english.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for something difficult or complicated to deal with.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a person, problem, situation, or task that is difficult to manage.
Use this when the emphasis is that the person, animal, or thing is difficult to handle rather than simply disobedient.
Use this when the troublesome thing is difficult to handle, fix, or get working, especially in casual speech.
Use this especially for a person or situation that is difficult to deal with or satisfy, rather than simply one with high standards.
Use this for the figurative sense of someone or something that is difficult to manage, work with, or use.
Use this colloquial choice when the task or problem is difficult to deal with or manage, rather than merely time-consuming.
Use this for a person or situation that is extremely difficult or frustrating to deal with.
Use this for a problem or situation that is difficult to handle, not for physical stickiness or humid weather.
Use this for a person or situation that is difficult, troublesome, or hard to deal with.
Use this when someone or something is particularly hard to deal with or manage.
